headline: Germany signs first bilateral CO2 export agreements with Denmark and the Netherlands
summary: At the Carbon Management Forum's Strategic Dialogue in Berlin (5-6 Oct), Germany signed its first government-to-government agreements allowing German industry to export CO2 for permanent sub-seabed storage under Denmark and the Netherlands. Germany bans onshore storage, so the deals open North Sea storage routes and are framed around enabling DACCS and BioCCS removals.
organisations: German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy
co2crc_note: Direct precedent for Australia-Timor-Leste (Bayu-Undan) cross-border CO2 export; shows the London Protocol Article 6 transboundary framework maturing into signed government-to-government deals.
extractor_note: Underlying signing 5-6 Oct 2026 at the Berlin Carbon Management Forum; out of the 7-8 Oct briefing window, carried as a radar near-miss. Carbon Pulse (Tier-1, paywalled) and Montel also reported.
